what: The /eth/ §5b chain figure, written by apps/eth/build.js; records stamped by sha256.
alt: In OpenAI’s environment (Lean v4.34.1), OpenAI’s statement implies a byte-for-byte copy of Anthropic’s ETHIsFalse (Hawkley’s chain, CERTIFIED, Lean’s kernel, nanoda); across the first version seam that copy is read as Anthropic’s statement, not decided. The chain beyond §5’s map. In Anthropic’s environment (Lean v4.33.1), Anthropic’s statement ETHIsFalse. In complexitylib’s environment (Lean v4.36.0-rc2), Anthropic’s proof, ported (47 of 809 files edited), proves the same file vendored byte for byte (the chain, CERTIFIED, Comparator, Lean’s kernel, nanoda, leanchecker --fresh): the second version seam is crossed by proof. complexitylib’s native proof implies ¬ETH on cslib’s multitape Turing machine with the binary encoding encCNF (D1, CERTIFIED, Lean’s kernel, nanoda, leanchecker --fresh), and ¬ETH on the word RAM with logarithmic words (C1, CERTIFIED, Comparator, Lean’s kernel, nanoda, leanchecker --fresh, every planted variant refused). The vendored ETHIsFalse implies the multitape ¬ETH (C2, CERTIFIED, Comparator, Lean’s kernel, nanoda, leanchecker --fresh, every planted variant refused). Both ¬ETH boxes link by dashed lines to the textbook statement, a reading of a definition. OpenAI’s proof with Hawkley’s two links, ported the same way (3,190 of 3,210 files unchanged), proves the same ETHIsFalse in complexitylib’s Lean (the OpenAI chain, CERTIFIED, Comparator, Lean’s kernel, nanoda, leanchecker --fresh, every planted variant refused; its judge tick from four named checkers), so no step on either side crosses a version seam.
